references.text: When Jacob heard that Joseph was alive, he was stunned and could not believe it – a parallel to the disciples' disbelief of joy over the risen Jesus. [ref:Gen 45:26]
The context just before this verse: Jesus appeared to the disciples, and they were terrified and frightened, thinking they saw a spirit. [ref:Luke 24:36-37]
Jesus' answer to the question in verse 41: the disciples gave him a piece of grilled fish, and he ate it before them to prove his bodily resurrection. [ref:Luke 24:42-43]
After the resurrection, Jesus asked the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias if they had anything to eat, a similar situation where the risen Jesus asks for food. [ref:John 21:5]
Also in John's account, Jesus showed the disciples his hands and his side, and they were glad when they saw the Lord – the joy of seeing the risen one. [ref:John 20:20]
Jesus gave physical proof of his resurrection by letting Thomas touch his wounds, just as he offered to eat here to show that he was truly present in bodily form. [ref:John 20:27]
Peter testified that they ate and drank with Jesus after the resurrection, which confirmed the bodily resurrection. [ref:Acts 10:41]
When Rhoda recognized Peter's voice, the others did not believe it out of joy – a parallel to being unable to believe from joy. [ref:Acts 12:14]
Earlier in the same chapter, the disciples did not believe the women's testimony about the resurrection – disbelief was a recurring theme among the disciples. [ref:Luke 24:11]
Mark tells that the disciples did not believe when they heard that Jesus had been seen alive – disbelief despite testimony of the resurrection. [ref:Mark 16:11]
